questions.q: Which value: Australia's society values equality of opportunity for all, regardless of background?
questions.a: True - equality and a fair go

questions.q: Is domestic and family violence against the law in Australia?
questions.a: Yes, it is against the law and should be reported to police

questions.q: In Australia, can you encourage violence against a person or group because of their culture or religion?
questions.a: No

questions.q: Do people in Australia have to follow an Australian value of mutual respect and tolerance for others?
questions.a: Yes

questions.q: Is it acceptable to refuse to rent a house to someone because of their race?
questions.a: No, discrimination based on race is against the law

questions.q: Should people in Australia make an effort to learn English?
questions.a: Yes, English is national language important for participation

questions.q: What pledge do new citizens make?
questions.a: Loyalty to Australia and its people, share democratic beliefs, respect rights and liberties, uphold and obey laws

questions.q: Is forced marriage allowed in Australia?
questions.a: No, it is against the law

questions.q: What does freedom of religion include in Australia?
questions.a: Freedom to follow any religion or no religion, but must obey law

questions.q: Does Australia allow freedom of speech to include inciting hatred against others?
questions.a: No, freedom does not include inciting hatred

questions.q: What is expected about participation in Australian society?
questions.a: Integrate, contribute, take responsibility, help when possible

questions.q: Is it important to support mateship and help others in times of crisis as in bushfire example?
questions.a: Yes, Australians come together in times of crisis

questions.q: What does secular mean in Australian society?
questions.a: Separate from religion, no official religion

questions.q: What is cyber abuse?
questions.a: Using technology to threaten, harass someone, against law

questions.q: What should you do about cyber abuse in Australia?
questions.a: Report to police and platform

questions.q: In Australia, can an employer refuse to hire someone because she is a woman?
questions.a: No, this is discrimination and is against the law
w: Yes, it is the employer's choice
Only if the boss prefers men
questions.e: It is against the law to discriminate against a person because of their gender. A person should get a job based on their skills and experience.

questions.q: Is it acceptable to use violence to settle a disagreement with your neighbour?
questions.a: No, violence is against the law
w: Only if no one sees it
questions.e: It is against the law to be violent towards another person. Australians believe in peaceful disagreement.

questions.q: Can a person in Australia be married to more than one person at the same time?
questions.a: No, polygamy is against the law
w: Only if their religion allows it
questions.e: Polygamy (being married to more than one person at the same time) is against the law in Australia and can result in severe penalties, including prison.

questions.q: What does mutual respect and tolerance mean in Australia?
questions.a: Listening to others and respecting their views, even when they are different from your own
w: Only respecting people from your own culture
Only respecting people who agree with you
questions.e: Mutual respect and tolerance means listening to others and respecting their views and opinions, even when they are different from your own.

questions.q: Do Australian laws apply to people from other cultures and backgrounds living in Australia?
questions.a: Yes, Australian laws apply to all people in Australia
w: No, they can follow the laws of their former country
questions.e: Australian laws apply to all people in Australia. Regardless of your background or culture, you must follow Australian laws.

questions.q: In Australia, who can make their own choices about personal matters such as marriage and religion?
questions.a: Both men and women
questions.e: Both men and women have the right to make their own independent choices about personal matters, such as marriage and religion.

questions.q: Is it acceptable to offer money to a police officer to avoid a fine?
questions.a: No, even offering a bribe to a police officer is a crime
questions.e: In Australia, it is a serious crime to bribe the police. It is a crime to even offer a bribe to a police officer.
